title: Target-Sum Slice

statement.markdown:
Given an integer array `nums` (values may be negative) and an integer `k`, decide whether any **non-empty contiguous** slice of the array sums exactly to `k`. Return `true` or `false`.

Negatives break the classic two-pointer shrink — you'll want prefix sums.

tests.note: empty array has no non-empty slice

hints: Let P(i) be the sum of the first i elements. A slice (i..j] sums to P(j) − P(i). What are you searching for?
Scanning with running sum s = P(j), you need some earlier prefix equal to s − k. Keep prefixes in a set.
Seed the set with 0 (the empty prefix) so slices starting at index 0 are found — and check BEFORE inserting s.
solutionExplanation: Prefix sums turn 'slice sums to k' into 'two prefixes differ by k'. Keep every prefix seen so far in a set; at each step check whether current − k was already a prefix. Seeding with 0 covers slices that start at the beginning, and checking before inserting keeps the slice non-empty. Time O(n), space O(n).
